headline: Africa's wildfire season is shrinking, satellite data shows
meta_description: Satellite imagery reveals Africa's burned land has steadily declined over the past two decades, with wildfire seasons arriving later.
summary_short: Satellite data shows the amount of land burned across Africa has been falling steadily over the past 20 years, bringing hope to the continent.
body:
Satellite imagery has revealed encouraging news: the amount of land burned by wildfires across Africa has been steadily falling over the past two decades. This steady decline signals a genuine shift in the continent's fire patterns.

The data shows that wildfire seasons are also arriving later in the year, which may be contributing to the reduction in burned acreage. This shift suggests natural cycles and management efforts may be working together to reduce the destructive impact of seasonal fires that have long threatened Africa's ecosystems and communities.

The long-term trend captured by satellites offers a rare piece of environmental good news, demonstrating that measurable progress is possible even in the face of climate pressures.
quick_facts: Burned land across Africa declining steadily over 20 years
Satellite data reveals shorter wildfire seasons continent-wide
Fire seasons now arriving later in the year
